title: Replace routing cache eviction with lock-free lease allocator and regional affinity decoupling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The current smart routing hotpath relies on a global mutex-protected LRU eviction cache for route metadata and a tight coupling between route affinity scoring and regional capacity checks. This has caused: increased tail latency under surge, lock contention in regional shards, and brittle failover ordering when a region experiences transient pressure.

Goal: Replace the mutexed eviction cache with a lock-free lease allocator that grants short-lived route leases to in-flight requests, and decouple affinity scoring from regional admission logic so scoring becomes a read-only input to allocation. This should reduce P99 routing latency, eliminate a class of deadlocks seen under compaction, and make fallback ordering more deterministic and testable.
acceptance_criteria: New lease allocator activated behind feature flag route_eviction_v2 and default off
P99 routing decision latency reduced by at least 10% on synthetic surge tests compared to baseline
No increased error rate (>0.1% delta) during gradual rollout to 30% of traffic
Regional affinity inputs are persisted as read-only snapshots; admission decisions no longer mutate affinity state
Audit log entries exist for lease grants/releases and appear in Console under routing->eviction with sample traces
Automated e2e tests covering lease expiry, lease-stealing, and inter-region failover pass in CI
tech_notes: Implementation in Rust module routing-core to avoid GC pauses; exposes a thin C++ FFI shim used by router process
Lease granularity: per-route-key with TTL 150ms default, configurable per-route class
Allocator algorithm: multi-producer, multi-consumer ring with epoch-based reclamation (EBR) to avoid locks
Affinity decoupling: introduce AffinitySnapshot produced by snapshotter, used read-only by allocator; snapshot updates pushed asynchronously to avoid hotpath writes
Telemetry: new counter route_eviction.lease_granted, route_eviction.lease_released, route_eviction.lease_stolen, and histogram route_eviction.grant_latency_ms
Fallback ordering: fallback candidates now sorted by stable priority + lease-age rather than live mutation, making deterministic replays possible
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: EBR reclamation window may hold memory longer under pathological churn; mitigated by aggressive epoch advance in allocator garbage collector
Risk: Rust FFI integration adds build complexity and requires cross-team CI adjustments; build image updated in ENG infra pipeline
Tradeoff: Read-only affinity snapshots mean very-stale scores could be used for a short window; snapshot TTL default 500ms chosen after benchmarks show minimal allocation regressions
Tradeoff: Lease TTL tuned to balance churn vs latency; may need further tuning per-customer workloads
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: RFC written and reviewed by Infra and Routing leads (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/routing/lease-allocator-rfc). Decided to prototype in Rust to contain memory behavior.
2026-02-25: Prototype allocator implemented and benchmarked in isolation: 40% reduction in mutex contention measured with synthetic 10k concurrent route lookups.
2026-03-02: FFI shim and initial integration into router process done; smoke tests pass in dev cluster. Observed 12% P99 latency improvement in dev surge profile.
2026-03-07: Design review with Security to confirm audit logging shape and ensure no sensitive fields are emitted. Security requested obfuscation of route keys in logs — implemented hashing layer.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout plan approved; feature flag implemented with safe kill-switch and metric gates defined. Preparing PR and CI jobs for review.
design_decisions: Choose lock-free EBR allocator over sharded mutex pools to simplify invariants and reduce tail lock contention
Persist only small AffinitySnapshot objects (<=512 bytes per route) to keep memory bounded
Telemetry exposed via existing statsd namespace routing.eviction to reuse dashboard infra
Fallbacks rely on stable candidate ordering to make canary comparisons meaningful: if two candidates have equal priority, prefer one with older lease to avoid livelock
testing_plan: Unit: Rust allocator unit tests for grant/release/steal and EBR reclamation
Integration: Router process with FFI shim executed in integration cluster under workload-sim (surge + regional outage)
E2E: Controlled canary on 5% -> 30% traffic with automated rollback if error_rate delta > 0.1% or P99 degrade > 5%
Chaos: Inject region latency skew and verify deterministic fallback ordering and graceful degradation
Performance: Run nightly benchmark suite and compare against baseline graphs in PerfDash
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge behind feature flag and enable in internal staging namespaces only
Phase 1: Canary on 5% traffic for 24 hours; run smoke assertions and manual inspection of routing.eviction metrics
Phase 2: Ramp to 30% over 48 hours if metrics stable; capture detailed traces for top 1% longest decisions
Phase 3: Global enable and remove old eviction code paths after 2 weeks of stable metrics
Rollback: feature flag off + restart router process, old mutexed cache remains available until final removal
links: Related tickets: ENG-31745 (orchestration interfaces), ENG-51234 (fallback executor isolation)
followups: Cleanup: remove legacy mutexed eviction code paths and config after 2 successful releases
Observability: add synthetic canary to alert if lease_stolen rate exceeds threshold
Policy: consider exposing per-customer lease tuning knobs in Console for Dedicated customers
